reason: Marisol asks for 40 miles and speedwork in the second week after a marathon. The draft answers both questions directly: "Not yet on either, but you're close." It backs that up with a stepped return for the 10K and an honest point that four weeks won't get her to her peak. The plan comes to about 21 easy miles with heart rate under 140. That's a sensible rise from her 12-mile recovery week and well under 40. The long run is 6 miles, so it isn't a sharp jump, and she keeps both of her usual rest days (Mon and Fri). Two sets of short strides are the only faster running, so this eases her back to consistency rather than bringing her back hard. It also respects how she feels without rushing her. Every day is clear enough to run as written. I took off a point because the stepped table is cut off in the review, so I can't check the later weeks. The Thanksgiving 10K date may also be a detail she never gave.
